notes: The Qing had conquered the last Ming loyalists by 1683.
Dutch Brazil ended in 1654.
The Khalkha Mongols submitted to the Qing in 1691; the west was the Dzungar Khanate.
Filled gaps in the source map from the nearest map (within 50 years).
Filled unclaimed land with peoples and cultures from neighbouring maps.
Named the remaining unclaimed regions after their regional peoples.

Bavaria, Saxony, Württemberg, the Electoral Palatinate and the other larger German states have their own territories inside the Holy Roman Empire, with outlines taken from the 1715, 1783, 1800 and 1815 maps; the smaller states stay in the Empire.
"Malaya" is a British-era name; the peninsula and its neighbours were Malay sultanates.
The Canary Islands were conquered by Castile by 1496; the Guanche territory is Castilian/Spanish here.
Hong Kong was part of Qing China until 1841; it no longer shows as a separate territory.
There was no Senegal before the French colony; the area was held by the Wolof and Fula kingdoms.
The British logwood cutters' settlements on the Bay of Honduras were called Belize only later.
The Funj Sultanate of Sennar (1504-1821) is on the map; its lands were drawn as Ottoman or Ethiopian.
Egypt was an Ottoman province, not a separate realm.
England took New Netherland in 1664 (finally in 1674): New York.
The Austronesian peoples of Taiwan and the islands were coloured as the Habsburg Monarchy.
The Dutch left Taiwan in 1662 and the Qing took the west of the island in 1683.
North Africa is named for its rulers of the time.
North American cultures are named for their time; the Mississippi and Ohio valleys were the land of the Mississippian and Fort Ancient cultures (boxes approximate).
Modern reservation, treaty and removal-era labels are replaced by the peoples who lived there at the time.
Plains peoples are shown where they lived at this date; the Comanche, Kiowa, Cheyenne and Lakota reached the southern and western Plains only in the 1700s.
Peoples and archaeological cultures are shown only while they existed.
Peoples are named and placed as they were at this date, not by modern reservations, treaties or regions.
Names respelled.
Colonies are shown as colonies, under the power that held them at this date, and only where it held them (lines approximate).
